prompt: How do you tell an intermediate operation from a terminal one?

choices.text: An intermediate one returns a `Stream`
choices.why: Right, and anything that returns something else ends the pipeline.

choices.text: Intermediate operations change the source collection
choices.why: No operation changes the source.

choices.text: Terminal operations are the ones written on the first line of the chain
choices.why: The terminal operation comes last.

choices.text: A terminal one takes a lambda; an intermediate one does not
choices.why: `filter` and `map` take lambdas and are intermediate.

prompt: In `Shelf.BOOKS.stream().filter(...).map(Book::title).toList()`, match each operation with what it returns.
hint: Only the last one returns something that is not a stream.

prompt: What does a stream built from `Shelf.BOOKS` hold?

choices.text: The results of every step, computed in advance
choices.why: Nothing is computed until the terminal operation.

choices.text: No data: a description of the work
choices.why: Right. The data stays in the list.

choices.text: An index into the list and nothing else, like a cursor in a database table
choices.why: It also holds the steps: what to keep and what to turn each into.

choices.text: A copy of the twelve books
choices.why: Nothing is copied; it reads the list as it goes.

prompt: `Stream.iterate(1, n -> n * 2).limit(10).toList()` finished. What would happen without `limit(10)`?

choices.text: It would stop at the largest `int`
choices.why: Overflow does not stop a stream; the values wrap around.

choices.text: `toList()` would keep pulling and never finish
choices.why: Right: until memory ran out.

choices.text: It would not compile
choices.why: It compiles; it is the run that never ends.

choices.text: It would collect ten values anyway, the default
choices.why: There is no default limit.

choices.text: `IntStream`
choices.why: Right, with `max`, `sum` and `average` built in.

choices.text: `Stream<Integer>`
choices.why: An `int[]` gives the primitive stream.

choices.text: `List<Integer>`
choices.why: A stream, not a list.

choices.text: `Stream<int[]>`
choices.why: That is `Stream.of(array)`, one element that is an array.

prompt: A pipeline has a source and two `peek` and `filter` steps, and no terminal operation. What does it print?

choices.text: One line per book
choices.why: That needs something to pull the books through.

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: Right: no terminal operation, no work.

choices.text: One line per book that passes the filter
choices.why: `peek` comes before `filter`, and neither ran.

choices.text: A compile error asking for a terminal operation
choices.why: It compiles, and silently does nothing.

prompt: With `findFirst`, how many books did the second pipeline of `Lazy.java` look at?
In the third pipeline, `upper: EMMA` was printed before `classic: Persuasion`. What does that show?

choices.text: Each element goes through every step before the next one starts
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: `peek` reorders the elements
choices.why: `peek` passes each element on unchanged.

choices.text: The output was printed out of order by two threads
choices.why: One thread; that is the real order.

choices.text: `map` runs before `filter` in every pipeline
choices.why: `filter` ran first on Emma; then `map` ran on Emma.

prompt: Which of these are short-circuiting, able to finish before the source is exhausted? Choose all that apply.
hint: They can stop once they know the answer.

choices.text: `anyMatch`
choices.why: Yes: the first match is enough.

choices.text: `findFirst`
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: `count`
choices.why: No: it has to see every element.

choices.text: `limit`
choices.why: Yes, as the third pipeline showed.

choices.text: `sorted`
choices.why: No: it must see everything before handing over the first.

prompt: `classics.count()` worked, and the second `classics.count()` threw. Which fix does the lesson suggest?
hint: Keep what can be traversed again.

choices.text: Use `peek` to copy the elements on the first pass
choices.why: `peek` is for looking, and copying is what the source already is.

choices.text: Catch the exception and use the first answer
choices.why: That hides the mistake rather than removing it.

choices.text: Call `classics.reset()` before the second count
choices.why: Streams have no `reset`.

choices.text: Keep the source and build a new stream for each question
choices.why: Right, or a `Supplier<Stream<Book>>` that builds one each time.

prompt: Why did `titles.add("Moby-Dick")` throw on a list from `toList()`?

choices.text: `toList()` returns an unmodifiable list
choices.why: Right. Wrap it in `new ArrayList<>(...)` to edit.

choices.text: `Moby-Dick` is not on the shelf
choices.why: Any string would have been refused.

choices.text: Lists of strings cannot grow past their first size in any Java version
choices.why: An `ArrayList` grows; this list is read-only by design.

choices.text: The stream was still open
choices.why: The stream had finished; the list is the problem.

prompt: The rule that a pipeline's lambdas must not change the source they read is called non-___.
hint: They must not get in its way.

prompt: A method stores `Stream<Book>` in a field so several other methods can use it. What will happen?

choices.text: It works, but slowly, because the stream is recomputed each time
choices.why: It is not recomputed; it is refused.

choices.text: Each method gets its own copy of the stream
choices.why: A field holds one object; there are no copies.

choices.text: The compiler rejects a stream stored in a field
choices.why: It compiles; the failure is at run time.

choices.text: The first terminal operation uses it up; the next one throws
choices.why: Right: `stream has already been operated upon or closed`.

prompt: Put the parts of `Shelf.BOOKS.stream().filter(...).map(Book::title).toList()` in the order they are written.
A pipeline sorts the shelf by price and then takes `findFirst`. How many books does it pull from the source?
hint: What does `sorted` need before it can hand over the first?

choices.text: None until a second terminal operation is called
choices.why: `findFirst` is the terminal operation, and it starts the work.

choices.text: One, because `findFirst` short-circuits
choices.why: `findFirst` stops early, but `sorted` has already pulled everything.

choices.text: All twelve
choices.why: Right: `sorted` must see every element first.

choices.text: Two: one to compare and one to return
choices.why: A sort compares far more than two.
